memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Asthma.
Symptoms: intermittent wheeze and exertional dyspnea over 3 months, nocturnal cough twice weekly. Examination: mild expiratory wheeze bilaterally, normal speech, no use of accessory muscles.
Spirometry: FEV1 2.2 L (65% predicted), FVC 2.8 L, FEV1/FVC 0.79. No prior test for change.
Asthma Control Test score 16 (not well controlled).
Technique checked: correct salbutamol metered-dose inhaler; budesonide-formoterol dry powder inhaler technique correct, inspiratory flow adequate.
Smoking status: never, pack-years 0.
Plan: start salbutamol MDI SOS, budesonide-formoterol 200/6 dry powder inhaler BD, montelukast 10 mg HS. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Salbutamol 100 mcg metered-dose inhaler, 2 puffs SOS.
Budesonide-formoterol 200/6 mcg dry powder inhaler, 2 puffs BD.
Montelukast sodium 10 mg tablet, 1 tablet HS.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Spirometry with reversibility.
Pre-bronchodilator: FEV1 2.2 L (65% pred), FVC 2.8 L, FEV1/FVC 0.79.
Post-bronchodilator (salbutamol 400 mcg): FEV1 2.5 L (73% pred), FVC 2.9 L, FEV1/FVC 0.86.
Reversibility: increase in FEV1 0.3 L (13%).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Allergic rhinitis to house dust mites: sneezing, nasal congestion, itchy eyes on exposure; confirmed by skin prick test.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Asthma.
Symptoms: reduced wheeze, nocturnal cough once weekly, able to climb two flights of stairs without dyspnea.
Examination: clear lungs, no wheeze.
Spirometry: FEV1 2.5 L (72% pred), FVC 3.0 L, FEV1/FVC 0.83; change in FEV1 since last test +0.3 L.
Asthma Control Test score 22 (well controlled).
Technique checked: correct for both inhalers; dry powder inspiratory flow >60 L/min.
Smoking status: never, pack-years 0.
Plan: continue current regimen; review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05

Spirometry.
FEV1 2.5 L (72% predicted), FVC 3.0 L, FEV1/FVC 0.83.
Change in FEV1 since previous test (+0.3 L).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Asthma exacerbation.
Symptoms: increased wheeze and nocturnal cough three nights/week, needed salbutamol 4 puffs daily for 5 days.
Examination: mild bilateral expiratory wheeze, normal speech.
Spirometry: FEV1 2.3 L (66% pred), FVC 2.9 L, FEV1/FVC 0.79; change in FEV1 since last test -0.2 L.
Asthma Control Test score 14 (not well controlled).
Technique checked: corrected salbutamol MDI technique (slow inhalation); budesonide-formoterol technique unchanged.
Smoking status: never, pack-years 0.
Plan: short course prednisolone 40 mg OD for 5 days, continue budesonide-formoterol BD, consider increasing to 400/12 if symptoms persist; review in 2 weeks.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Prednisolone 10 mg tablet, 4 tablets OD for 5 days.
Salbutamol 100 mcg metered-dose inhaler, 2 puffs SOS.
Budesonide-formoterol 200/6 mcg dry powder inhaler, 2 puffs BD.
Montelukast sodium 10 mg tablet, 1 tablet HS.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Asthma.
Symptoms: asymptomatic, no nocturnal cough, able to jog 2 km without dyspnea.
Examination: clear lungs.
Spirometry: FEV1 2.4 L (69% pred), FVC 3.0 L, FEV1/FVC 0.80; change in FEV1 since last test +0.1 L.
Asthma Control Test score 24 (well controlled).
Technique checked: correct for both inhalers; dry powder inspiratory flow adequate.
Smoking status: never, pack-years 0.
Plan: discontinue montelukast; continue salbutamol SOS and budesonide-formoterol BD; review in 3 months.
